title: State v. Tucker (N.J. 1994)
key_points: Holding: Under the NJ Constitution, a person is seized when an officer's words or actions would make a reasonable person believe they are not free to leave, even if they have not submitted. Flight alone, without reasonable suspicion beforehand, did not justify the chase.
officer_notes: Scenario: You chase a teen who ran when your car turned the corner, with no other suspicious facts. He drops drugs during the chase.
Takeaway: In NJ the chase can be the seizure; you need reasonable suspicion before you pursue.
